description: Stellavion is an independent team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Driven by curiosity and innovation, we aim to transform scientific ideas into practical solutions through technology, creativity and exploration.
summary:
MarsGuard is an interactive, terrain-aware route-planning application developed by Team Stellavion for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Designed for the Jezero Crater region of Mars, MarsGuard uses real NASA elevation datasets to help users explore Martian terrain and compare possible travel routes.

The application uses the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate two routes: a shortest-distance route and a slope-aware alternative that penalizes steeper terrain. Users can select starting and destination points, adjust terrain preferences, and compare distance, elevation changes, slopes, and calculated route costs.

MarsGuard integrates elevation data from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter's Context Camera (CTX) digital elevation model for local terrain analysis, while Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) data provides regional elevation context.

By visualizing the trade-off between shorter routes and less steep terrain, MarsGuard demonstrates how real planetary data and explainable algorithms can support future Mars exploration planning. It is a research prototype, not a certified navigation or safety system.
details:
What MarsGuard Does

MarsGuard is a web-based Martian terrain exploration and route-planning prototype focused on Jezero Crater. It allows users to explore real NASA elevation data, select two locations, and compare different routes across the terrain.

How It Works

MarsGuard uses the A* pathfinding algorithm on a 20-metre CTX digital elevation grid.

The application calculates two routes:

  • Shortest-distance route: Minimizes horizontal travel distance.
  • Slope-aware route: Applies an adjustable penalty to steeper terrain, allowing users to explore alternative paths.

Users can adjust the slope penalty and compare horizontal distance, elevation gain and loss, maximum slope, average slope, and route cost. Both routes are evaluated using a common cost model to make the comparison explainable.

NASA Data Integration

MarsGuard uses two real planetary datasets:

  • CTX DEM: Provides local terrain elevation and slope information for route calculations.
  • MOLA: Provides regional elevation context for exploring the wider Martian landscape.

MOLA does not contribute directly to the route calculation.

Technologies Used

The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, NumPy, and Rasterio/GDAL for geospatial processing and route calculations.

The application is deployed using Vercel and Render.

Innovation and Benefits

MarsGuard goes beyond displaying a Martian map by allowing users to investigate how terrain steepness changes route selection. Its adjustable routing model and measurable comparisons help users understand the trade-off between travel distance and terrain difficulty.

Limitations and Future Impact

MarsGuard is a research prototype limited to Jezero Crater. It does not incorporate live Martian conditions, small-scale obstacles, or astronaut safety requirements.

The project demonstrates how accessible NASA datasets and explainable route-planning algorithms can contribute to future planetary exploration research and educational applications.

AI Assistance Disclosure

AI tools assisted with project planning, research, coding, testing, and documentation. aThe demonstration video uses AI-generated English narration created with Microsoft Clipchamp. MarsGuard's route calculations use a deterministic A* algorithm, not a generative AI model.
